legal.hit: My landlord has served me a Section 21 notice giving me two months to leave, but I'm not even sure it's been filled in correctly. What are my options here, and do I have to go by the date they've put?
legal.near: My landlord served me a Section 21 notice, but it turned out the dates were filled in wrong so it wasn't valid, and the council's housing team confirmed I didn't have to leave. Sharing in case anyone else gets one that looks off.

legal.hit: There's been damp spreading across my bedroom wall for months and the landlord keeps ignoring my emails about repairs. How do I push this forward, and what can I actually make them do?
legal.near: There was damp spreading across my bedroom wall for months and the landlord ignored every repair request, but after I logged it with environmental health they finally sorted it. Just flagging that the route works.

legal.hit: I was let go the day after I raised a complaint about my manager, with no warning or process at all. Does this count as unfair dismissal, and how long do I have to do something about it?
legal.near: I was let go the day after raising a complaint, but I took it to an employment tribunal and they ruled it was unfair dismissal, with a settlement paid last week. Posting so others know the time limits are tighter than you'd think.

legal.hit: My old employer still hasn't paid my final month's wages and now isn't answering the phone. Where do I start with getting what I'm owed?
legal.near: My old employer withheld my final month's wages, but a quick letter mentioning the small claims route got the full amount transferred within a fortnight. Sharing the template that worked for me.

legal.hit: I bought a washing machine eight months ago and it's already packed in, but the shop says it's out of warranty. Under consumer rights, am I entitled to a repair or refund here?
legal.near: My washing machine packed in at eight months and the shop fobbed me off, but once I quoted the Consumer Rights Act they arranged a free replacement. Glad I dug my heels in.

legal.hit: I cancelled a rolling contract in writing but they're still taking payments and claim I'm tied in for another year. Can they hold me to a contract I've already given notice on?
legal.near: They kept taking payments after I cancelled my rolling contract, but my bank reversed them under the direct debit guarantee once I showed the notice I'd sent. Just passing on what sorted it.

legal.hit: A debt collector is chasing me for a catalogue account I genuinely don't recognise from years ago. Do I have to pay this, and how do I make them prove it's mine?
legal.near: A debt collector chased me for an old catalogue account I didn't recognise, but when I sent a 'prove the debt' request they couldn't produce the agreement and dropped it. Sharing because so many people just pay up.

legal.hit: My ex and I are splitting up and we can't agree on the children's arrangements. Where do we even begin, and is mediation something we have to try first?
legal.near: My ex and I couldn't agree on the children's arrangements, but a few sessions of mediation got us to a parenting plan without ever going near a court. Recommending it to anyone dreading the process.

legal.hit: My father died without a will and my stepmother is saying she gets everything. Under the rules of intestacy, where do his children actually stand?
legal.near: My father died without a will and my stepmother assumed she'd get it all, but the rules of intestacy meant his children were entitled to a share too, now all settled. Noting it in case it helps someone.

legal.hit: My neighbour has put up a new fence that I'm sure is a good foot onto my land. How do I check the boundary properly, and what can I do if I'm right?
legal.near: My neighbour put a fence a foot onto my land, but pulling the title plan from the Land Registry settled the boundary and they moved it back. Sharing in case anyone's mid-argument over a fence.

legal.hit: My settled status seems to have dropped to pre-settled when I checked the online portal, and I've lived here twelve years. How do I get this corrected?
legal.near: My status showed as pre-settled by mistake despite twelve years here, but uploading my old tenancy and payslips got it upgraded to settled status within a month. Posting the document list that worked.

legal.hit: Someone's been posting false claims about my business on a local Facebook group, saying I rip people off. Is there anything I can do about this kind of thing?
legal.near: Someone posted false claims about my business on a local group, but a firmly worded letter pointing out it was defamatory got the posts taken down and an apology. Just letting traders know it's worth a shot.

legal.hit: A builder took a deposit, did half the job badly and then vanished. Is the small claims court the right route for getting my money back, and how much does it cost to file?
legal.near: A builder took my deposit and vanished, but I filed in the small claims court and got a judgment plus my fee back. Sharing how straightforward the online process actually was.

legal.hit: We want to put a single-storey extension on the back of the house. Do we need full planning permission for that, or does it fall under permitted development?
legal.near: We weren't sure our extension needed planning permission, but a lawful development certificate confirmed it fell under permitted development. Flagging that the certificate is worth getting for peace of mind.

legal.hit: My home insurer is refusing to pay out on a burst pipe claim, saying it's 'wear and tear'. Is there a way to challenge that decision?
legal.near: My insurer rejected my burst-pipe claim as 'wear and tear', but escalating to the Financial Ombudsman overturned it and they paid in full. Sharing because the first 'no' clearly isn't final.

legal.hit: I've got a parking charge from a private car park for overstaying by four minutes in a free space. Do I actually have to pay these, and is it worth appealing?
legal.near: I got a private parking charge for overstaying by four minutes, but I appealed to POPLA and it was cancelled. Passing on that the appeal stage is free and worth using.

legal.hit: My PIP claim got turned down even though my condition's got worse. How do I challenge it, and is mandatory reconsideration the first step?
legal.near: My PIP claim was refused despite things getting worse, but a mandatory reconsideration with extra evidence overturned it. Sharing the bit of advice that turned it around — get a supporting letter in.

legal.hit: They've made me redundant after six years but I don't think the consultation was done properly. What am I entitled to, and could this have been handled unlawfully?
legal.near: I was made redundant after six years with a rushed consultation, but challenging the process got me an improved redundancy package. Noting that it's worth questioning rather than just signing.

legal.hit: Our flight was cancelled the night before and the airline is only offering a voucher, not cash. Are we entitled to a proper refund and any compensation?
legal.near: Our flight was cancelled and the airline pushed a voucher, but citing the passenger rights rules got us a full cash refund plus compensation. Sharing the form reference that did it.

legal.hit: A builder is now demanding double his original written quote for the same work. Can he hold me to a price way above what we agreed in writing?
legal.near: A builder tried to charge double his written quote, but pointing out the agreed figure in the contract held him to the original price. Glad I kept everything in writing.

legal.hit: My landlord changed the locks while I was at work and put my things outside, with no notice at all. Is he allowed to do that, and what do I do tonight?
legal.near: My landlord changed the locks and dumped my things outside, but the council confirmed it was an illegal eviction and the police had him let me back in that evening. Sharing the emergency number that helped.

legal.hit: Bailiffs are threatening to come round over council tax arrears that I'm already paying off in instalments. Can they still turn up if I've got an arrangement?
legal.near: Bailiffs threatened to visit over council tax arrears, but once I showed the arrangement I'd already set up, the visit was called off. Letting people know an existing payment plan does count.

legal.hit: We're divorcing and my ex wants to keep the house outright, even though it was bought together. How is the property usually divided, and do I need a consent order?
legal.near: We divorced and sorted the house between us, and getting a consent order sealed by the court made the financial settlement final and clean. Recommending the consent order so nothing reopens later.

legal.hit: I'm executor of my aunt's will but one of the beneficiaries is disputing everything and stalling probate. What are my duties here, and how do I move probate along?
legal.near: As executor I had a beneficiary disputing everything, but a clear letter setting out my duties and the probate timeline settled them down, and we've now distributed the estate. Sharing what calmed it.

legal.hit: My neighbour runs power tools in his garden until midnight most nights. What's the proper way to deal with persistent noise like this?
legal.near: My neighbour ran power tools till midnight for weeks, but a noise diary logged with environmental health got it stopped under a nuisance notice. Sharing because the diary was the key bit.

legal.hit: A job offer has been pulled because the employer says they can't verify my right to work, even though I've got status. How do I prove it to them properly?
legal.near: An employer doubted my right to work, but generating a share code from the Home Office portal proved my status and the offer stood. Posting because not everyone knows the share code exists.

legal.hit: A former tenant has left a string of untrue reviews accusing me of theft. Can I get these removed, and is threatening to chase it the only way?
legal.near: A former tenant left untrue reviews accusing me of theft, but reporting them as defamatory to the platform got them removed without it ever escalating. Just flagging the report route worked.

legal.hit: A client owes me £1,800 for completed work and keeps stalling. Is small claims worth it for that amount, and what do I need before I file?
legal.near: A client owed me £1,800 and kept stalling, but a letter before action warning of small claims got me paid the next week. Sharing that the warning letter often does the job on its own.

legal.hit: We've had a planning enforcement notice about a porch the previous owners built without permission. Are we liable for what they did, and can we apply retrospectively?
legal.near: We got a planning enforcement notice over a porch the previous owners built, but a retrospective application was approved and the notice withdrawn. Noting that retrospective permission is a real option.

legal.hit: My insurer has written off my car after a crash and the payout is way below what I'd pay to replace it. Can I dispute the valuation they've put on it?
legal.near: My insurer's write-off payout was well below replacement value, but sending three like-for-like adverts got them to raise the offer. Sharing the trick that pushed the valuation up.

legal.hit: Universal Credit say I've been overpaid and want it all back at once, but the mistake was theirs. Do I have to repay it, and can I ask for smaller deductions?
legal.near: Universal Credit demanded a lump-sum repayment for their own overpayment error, but requesting affordable deductions spread it out painlessly. Letting people know you can ask for the rate to be lowered.

legal.hit: I've had a penalty charge notice for a bus lane I'm sure I never entered — the photo is hard to make out. How do I challenge a PCN like this?
legal.near: I got a bus-lane penalty charge notice but the photo didn't actually show my car in the lane, and a formal challenge to the council cancelled it. Sharing that asking for the footage is worth doing.

medical.hit: I've had a chesty cough for nearly three weeks now and it's just not shifting. Is this something I should get seen about, or just ride out?
medical.near: I had a chesty cough for nearly three weeks, but the GP listened to my chest, said it was viral and it cleared on its own. Thanks to whoever recommended honey and lemon — it helped.

medical.hit: My toddler has come out in a blotchy red rash overnight but seems well in himself. Should I be worried about this, and does the glass test apply here?
medical.near: My toddler came out in a blotchy rash overnight, but the GP confirmed it was just a viral one and it faded in a couple of days. Sharing so other nervous parents know it's usually nothing.

medical.hit: My lower back has seized up badly since lifting some boxes and I can barely stand straight. Is it safe to keep moving, or should I be resting it?
medical.near: My lower back seized after lifting boxes, but the pharmacist suggested anti-inflammatories and gentle movement and I was upright again in a few days. Passing on what worked for me.

medical.hit: I keep getting dizzy spells when I stand up too quickly and it's happening more often. What might be behind this, and when should I get it checked?
medical.near: I kept getting dizzy on standing, but the GP checked my blood pressure, tweaked one of my tablets and the spells have stopped. Glad I mentioned it rather than ignoring it.

medical.hit: I've found a small lump under my arm that's been there a couple of weeks. How soon should I get this looked at, and is it likely to be anything?
medical.near: I found a small lump under my arm, but the GP examined it, said it was a harmless cyst and it's already going down. Posting to reassure anyone who's found something and is panicking.

medical.hit: One of my ankles has swollen up over the last few days but the other one's completely fine. Is one-sided swelling something I need seen quickly?
medical.near: One ankle swelled up out of nowhere, but the GP ruled out anything serious and it was down to standing all day at work. Thanks for the suggestions about keeping it elevated.

medical.hit: I've been given a new prescription but I'm already on blood pressure tablets. Is it okay to take them together, or should I space them out?
medical.near: I was worried my new prescription would clash with my blood pressure tablets, but the pharmacist checked and said they're fine together. Sharing that the pharmacy will always check for you.

medical.hit: I forgot to take my antibiotics this morning and it's now nearly time for the next dose. Do I double up, or just skip the missed one?
medical.near: I missed a dose of my antibiotics and panicked, but the pharmacist said to just carry on with the next one and not double up. Noting it in case anyone else does the same.

medical.hit: My little one has had a temperature of 39 for a day now and isn't eating. At what point should I take her to be seen rather than managing at home?
medical.near: My little one ran a temperature of 39 for a day, but she perked up after fluids and Calpol and the GP was happy it was viral. Thanks to the parents here who talked me down.

medical.hit: My home monitor keeps reading my blood pressure at around 150 over 95. Is that high enough to act on, and should I be booking in about it?
medical.near: My home monitor kept showing around 150 over 95, but the GP did a proper set of readings, started me on a low dose and it's come right down. Glad I didn't just ignore the numbers.

medical.hit: My blood test came back saying my cholesterol is raised but no one's rung me about it. Should I be doing something now, or waiting for them to call?
medical.near: My blood test flagged raised cholesterol, but the GP went through it with me and a few diet changes plus a statin have sorted it. Sharing that it's worth booking a review to talk results through.

medical.hit: I've barely slept properly for weeks now and it's really affecting me in the day. Is this worth seeing someone about, or are there things I should try first?
medical.near: I went weeks barely sleeping, but the GP talked me through sleep hygiene and a short course of help and I'm finally resting. Passing on that they took it seriously rather than dismissing it.

medical.hit: I caught my hand on a rusty nail and it's a deepish cut. Do I need a tetanus jab for this, and should it be looked at?
medical.near: I caught my hand on a rusty nail, but A&E cleaned it, gave me a tetanus booster and it's healing fine. Thanks for the nudge to get it seen rather than leaving it.

medical.hit: I've been feeling low and anxious for a couple of months now and it's just not lifting. How do I go about getting some help with this?
medical.near: I felt low and anxious for months, but self-referring to the talking therapies service got me sessions that genuinely helped. Sharing the self-referral link because you don't need the GP to do it for you.

medical.hit: I'm getting frequent throbbing headaches with light sensitivity a few times a week now. Could these be migraines, and what should I do about them?
medical.near: My throbbing headaches with light sensitivity turned out to be migraines, and the GP sorted a preventative that's cut them right down. Sharing that keeping a trigger diary really helped the appointment.

medical.hit: A mole on my back seems to have changed shape and colour over the last few months. How quickly should I get this checked out?
medical.near: A mole on my back had changed shape, but the GP looked at it under a scope, said it was benign and is keeping an eye on it. Posting to nudge anyone hesitating to just get it seen.

medical.hit: I've had on-and-off stomach pain and bloating for weeks after eating. Is this something to mention to the doctor, or just food-related?
medical.near: I had weeks of stomach pain and bloating, but the GP ran tests, found nothing sinister and a few diet tweaks settled it. Glad I got it checked rather than worrying in silence.

medical.hit: One of my eyes has gone red and a bit gritty for a few days with some discharge. Will this clear on its own, or do I need drops from somewhere?
medical.near: My eye went red and gritty, but the pharmacist took a look and recommended drops that cleared it within days — no GP needed. Sharing that the pharmacy handles a lot of this now.

medical.hit: I've had a really sore throat for over a week and it's painful to swallow. Is it worth getting antibiotics for, or will it pass?
medical.near: I had a sore throat for over a week, but the pharmacist's throat-check scheme said it was viral so no antibiotics, and it passed. Noting that the pharmacy scheme saved me a GP appointment.

medical.hit: Since starting a new tablet I've had constant nausea and headaches. Is this likely a side effect I should report, and can I just stop taking it?
medical.near: My new tablet gave me nausea and headaches, but the GP swapped me to a different one and I'm fine now. Sharing that you shouldn't just stop — they sorted an alternative quickly.

medical.hit: I keep getting a fluttering feeling in my chest, mostly in the evenings. Is this the kind of thing I should get checked, or is it harmless?
medical.near: I kept getting chest flutters in the evenings, but an ECG at the clinic showed nothing worrying and it was put down to caffeine. Glad I had it checked for the reassurance.

medical.hit: My ear's been blocked and a bit painful for several days and my hearing's muffled. Should I get it syringed, or could this be an infection?
medical.near: My ear was blocked and muffled for days, but the GP spotted an infection and a short course of treatment cleared it. Passing on that I'd wrongly assumed it was just wax.

medical.hit: My son's had a barking cough and his breathing sounds wheezy at night. When does a cough like this need a doctor rather than home care?
medical.near: My son had a barking, wheezy cough, but the out-of-hours GP checked him over, said it was croup and talked us through managing it at home. Thanks to everyone who reassured us overnight.

medical.hit: My knee's been swollen and stiff for a couple of weeks with no injury I can think of. Should I get this seen, and what might cause it?
medical.near: My knee was swollen and stiff for weeks with no injury, but the GP examined it, sent me for a scan and it's being managed well now. Sharing that 'no injury' doesn't mean it's not worth a look.

medical.hit: I'm pregnant and have had some cramping and a bit of spotting today. Is this something I should get checked urgently, or is it common?
medical.near: I had cramping and spotting in pregnancy, but the midwife at the early pregnancy unit checked everything and all was well. Sharing the direct number because it saved a panicked trip to A&E.

medical.hit: I've been really thirsty and tired and weeing a lot lately. Are these the kind of symptoms I should get a blood test for?
medical.near: I'd been thirsty, tired and weeing constantly, but a blood test at the GP caught my blood sugar early and it's now being managed. Posting because I nearly brushed the symptoms off.

medical.hit: My repeat prescription has run out and my regular tablets are due. What's the quickest way to get a fresh supply sorted?
medical.near: My repeat prescription ran out, but the pharmacy's urgent supply service got me enough tablets to bridge the gap until the GP renewed it. Flagging that service for anyone caught short.

medical.hit: I've got a sharp pain in the bottom of my heel that's worst first thing in the morning. Any idea what this is, and should I see someone?
medical.near: My sharp heel pain first thing turned out to be plantar fasciitis, and the GP's stretches and insoles have nearly fixed it. Sharing because I'd never have guessed what it was.

medical.hit: I keep coming out in hives after meals but can't pin down the cause. Should I be seeing someone about a possible allergy?
medical.near: I kept getting hives after meals, but the GP referred me to an allergy clinic and we've narrowed down the trigger. Sharing that it's worth pushing for the referral if it keeps happening.

medical.hit: I've been exhausted for weeks no matter how much I sleep. Is this worth a trip to the doctor, and what might they test for?
medical.near: I was exhausted for weeks despite sleeping, but a GP blood test found low iron and a supplement has me feeling human again. Glad I went rather than assuming it was just life.

medical.hit: A small cut on my leg has gone red, hot and swollen over the last day. Does this look like it's getting infected, and should I be seen today?
medical.near: A small cut on my leg went red and hot, but the GP started me on antibiotics straight away and it settled quickly. Noting that the same-day appointment line was the right call.

medical.hit: I've had some floaters and flashes in one eye since this morning. Is this an urgent thing, or something that settles on its own?
medical.near: I had sudden floaters and flashes, but the eye clinic saw me the same day, checked my retina and all was fine. Sharing that they treat this as urgent — don't sit on it.
